comments.author: suryabdev
comments.body:
Hi @daxton256, the `LocalPythonExecutor` requires base Python tools ([BASE_PYTHON_TOOLS](https://github.com/huggingface/smolagents/blob/06cfa27051837fd41830b79ac4338e7f4cf0edd9/src/smolagents/local_python_executor.py#L71)) like range, print etc to be passed explicitly
They are initialized to None
https://github.com/huggingface/smolagents/blob/06cfa27051837fd41830b79ac4338e7f4cf0edd9/src/smolagents/local_python_executor.py#L1655
You can use the `send_tools` function to add them. The following code will work
```
from smolagents import LocalPythonExecutor
executor = LocalPythonExecutor([])
executor.send_tools({})
print(executor("for i in range(1,3):\n\tprint(i)"))

# CodeOutput(output=None, logs='1\n2\n', is_final_answer=False)
```

Alternatively, You could use the `PythonInterpreterTool`, that will add the base tools automatically and use `LocalPythonExecutor`
```
from smolagents import PythonInterpreterTool
tool = PythonInterpreterTool()
print(tool("for i in range(1,3):\n\tprint(i)"))

# Stdout:
# 1
# 2
# 
# Output: None
```

comments.author: albertvillanova
comments.body: Yes, as @daxton256 already explained, the issue comes from not using `LocalPythonExecutor` in the intended way.
